objects: E is the fixed position space; V is a real-valued globally C2 potential; alpha and beta are nonnegative real parameters and eta is a real parameter. mu is literally canonical-volume.tilted(-V). J is literally the pushforward of mu.prod(stdGaussian E) by (x,z) -> (x,x+sqrt(eta) scalar-multiplied by z), nu is literally its second marginal, and S(y) is literally canonical-volume tilted by -V((y+u)/2)-||y-u||^2/(8 eta). Tf is the real Bochner integral of the observer f against this S(y). G is a real-linear partial map of the displayed scalar-to-vector L2 spaces, and G.closure is its actual closure. There are no caller-selected laws, normalizers, conditional versions, gradient certificates, or alternative representatives in these definitions.
domains: E is finite-dimensional over R, with its given real norm/inner product and Borel measurable structure; rank zero is allowed. V and every f and phi are globally defined on E. x and Hessian-direction v range independently over all E. Both Lp spaces use exponent 2 and precisely the same literal nu; they consist of AE classes of strongly measurable square-integrable scalar or E-valued functions and need not be finite-dimensional. G.domain is a linear subspace dense in all Lp R 2 nu. G.graph and G.closure.graph are subsets of the product of those two Lp spaces. y and the S-integral variable u range over E. Smooth compact support is required of phi and f, with no sign or centering restriction; compact support is not required of Tf.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E and all displayed structures, V : E -> R, alpha,beta : R_{>=0}, eta : R, and proofs of exactly the six assumptions. Within the Hessian assumption universally quantify x,v : E. mu,J,nu,S are subsequent fixed let-bound objects. Conclude IsProbabilityMeasure nu AND an existential G. Inside this one existential, assert density, closability, closedness, then universally quantify all pairs of Lp classes u,v for the graph biconditional; its smooth compact phi is existential and may depend on u,v. Still inside this same G existential, universally quantify f and its smoothness/compact-support proofs, let-bind Tf from f, and existentially supply hTf then hGrad with the canonical graph-membership conclusion. G may depend on the ambient input data, but is chosen before and uniformly for all f and all graph pairs.
assumptions: Exactly: NormedAddCommGroup E; InnerProductSpace R E; FiniteDimensional R E; MeasurableSpace E; BorelSpace E; V : E -> R; alpha,beta : R_{>=0}; eta : R; 0 < (alpha : R); alpha <= beta; ContDiff R 2 V; forall x,v : E, (alpha : R)*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v AND (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v <= (beta : R)*||v||^2; 0 < eta; (beta : R)*eta <= 1. The observer branch separately assumes ContDiff R infinity f and HasCompactSupport f. No caller-provided density, closability, law/normalizer, conditional representative, derivative-integral interchange, or output L2 premise is added.
conclusion: For the literal nu, IsProbabilityMeasure nu and there exists G : LinearPMap R (Lp R 2 nu) (Lp E 2 nu) with Dense G.domain, G.IsClosable, and G.closure.IsClosed. For every Lp pair, membership in G.graph is equivalent to existence of one globally smooth compactly supported scalar phi simultaneously representing the input and its genuine gradient representing the output nu-AE. For every globally smooth compactly supported f, the literal Tf and gradient(Tf) each satisfy MemLp at exponent 2 under nu, and their proof-independent canonical classes form a pair in that same G.closure.graph. Closure membership is of the exact actual pair, not of a caller-supplied substitute vector field.
scopes: The graph characterization is an exhaustive biconditional, not merely an inclusion or a premise requiring a supplied certificate. Closability and closedness concern the product-Lp graph topology; the domain-density assertion concerns the entire scalar Lp space. Closure membership is the canonical approximation/closed-extension relation supplied by this partial-map graph; no separate weak-H1 equivalence is asserted. The theorem does not explicitly assert probability status of mu or every S(y), even though those objects are normalized tilts by definition. It does not assert pointwise or uniform estimates, a quantitative derivative bound, that Tf has compact support, higher smoothness of Tf, a formula for gradient(Tf), differentiation under the integral, arbitrary rough-observer regularity, conditional-disintegration identities, dynamics, convergence rates, discretization errors, or query costs. No unique G, rate constant, or scalar norm bound is separately quantified.
constant_dependencies: No new numerical constant is existentially introduced. The literal constants 1/2 and 8 and the exponent 2 are fixed. alpha,beta,eta obey the displayed restrictions; eta appears in sqrt(eta) in J and 8*eta in S. The existential G may depend on E,V,alpha,beta,eta and the ambient structures and hypotheses, but is uniform over f. Tf depends on f and on the fixed S; MemLp proof witnesses may depend on f. Any phi in the graph characterization depends on its particular Lp pair. No additional derivative bounds or dependencies are inferred.
